subject: Clarifying evidence for HealthOps SIG: prompt/log retention and training opt-out
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthops.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the SIG spreadsheet you sent earlier. Our security team had a few follow-ups on the data-handling section before we finalize:

- Can you confirm the retention windows for prompt/request logs, KV cache, and any operational traces? Our draft shows a 7-day window but we'd like exact language.
- Do you ever use customer prompts or responses for model training or improvement? If so, under what circumstances and what opt-out controls do customers have?
- For KV cache or session-level caches, please clarify whether any part of the cache is ever persisted or included in backups.

I've attached our filled SIG template (HealthOps_SIG_Template.xlsx). If you can provide a short evidence packet (SOC2, a sample redaction playbook, and concise SIG answer copy) that would be ideal. Our deadline for the SIG submission is EOD next Friday (2026-02-19).

Appreciate a short call if that's easier — we can do 30 minutes.

Best,
Elena
Security Operations
HealthOps Inc.

Attachment: HealthOps_SIG_Template.xlsx
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthops.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Elena —

Thanks for the detailed template. Quick answers up front and attached evidence below. I also included laura and soojin for any compliance-level clarifications.

Summary (short):
- Prompt/request logs: Operational logs (request metadata and full prompt/response) are persisted for up to 14 days by default to support debugging and incident analysis. After 14 days those logs are purged from our short-term storage.
- KV/session cache: KV caches are ephemeral and live in GPU memory; we do not persist KV cache to long-term storage or backups. Caches are flushed at session termination or after 2 hours of inactivity.
- Training on customer data: We do NOT use customer prompt/response data for model training or model improvements unless the customer has explicitly opted in via contract and account-level setting. For customers who opt in, data used for training is isolated and processed through our secure training ingestion pipeline with additional review and redaction steps.

Attached evidence: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf (redacted), redwood_SIG_evidence_package.zip (sample logs with redaction markers, retention config screenshots, and the internal playbook excerpt). I've also uploaded the same package to our shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_redwood_evidence

Suggested next steps:
- I can paste suggested SIG answer text into the spreadsheet and return it (or send as a Word doc).
- If you'd like a 20–30 minute walkthrough of the artifacts, we can do Wed or Thu morning PST.

Notes for SIG wording: we typically recommend explicit language like:
"Redwood retains request-level logs (prompts and responses) for a default period of 14 days for operational troubleshooting. Request-level data is not used for model training unless the customer has expressly opted in via contract and account settings; otherwise data is not included in training datasets."

Happy to tighten wording based on your legal/security preferences.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_SIG_evidence_package.zip, SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthops.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Thanks — that helps a lot. Quick clarifications:

On your note you mention 14 days for request logs; our internal intake doc referenced a 7-day default in one row. Can you confirm 14 days is the canonical default and whether any customers are still on older 7-day buckets?

Also, the exact line you suggested looks good but we need to make sure the SIG answer is unambiguous about opt-out. Can you provide a one-sentence "opt-out" clause we can paste directly into the template?

If you can attach the suggested spreadsheet entry as a Word snippet or the template cell text, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Elena

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:02 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Thanks for the detailed template. Quick answers up front and attached evidence below...

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@healthops.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Elena — following up with canonical language and a pasted answer you can drop into the SIG template. We confirmed with ops: 14 days is the current default for persisted request logs; we migrated all customers off the older 7-day bucket by 2025-11-01 during our logging consolidation. No customers remain on 7-day.

Suggested SIG answer (paste into the SIG cell):
"Redwood retains request-level logs (which may include prompt and model-generated response text) for a default period of 14 days to support operational troubleshooting and security investigations. KV/session caches are ephemeral and are not persisted to backups; caches are flushed at session end or after 2 hours of inactivity. Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses for model training unless the customer has explicitly opted in via contract and an account-level opt-in flag. Customers may request exclusion from data retention and training by contacting their account team; exclusion requests are implemented within 5 business days unless a contract specifies otherwise"

Attached: HealthOps_SIG_answers_v2.docx (word snippet with the above line placed in the correct template cell), SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf (redacted). I've also published the final evidence zip to our support artifact store and included the link in the template: https://app.redwood.com/controls/sig-evidence/HEALTHOPS-4827

If that language works, I'll save a signed copy of the spreadsheet and close this loop. Happy to hop on a call if you'd like to walk the wording live.

Best,
Michael
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
